address_cn: 张家界市永定区大庸路天门山索道公司下站
hook: The world's longest cable car soars 7.5 kilometers over the city into the clouds, delivering you to a mountain where a natural hole through the cliff face forms 'Heaven's Gate,' glass skywalks cling to vertical rock faces, and a road with 99 hairpin turns snakes up 1,300 meters.
honest_description: Tianmen Mountain is Zhangjiajie's adrenaline attraction — a spectacular combination of engineering marvels and natural wonders that delivers genuine thrills. The 7.5 km cable car ride from downtown Zhangjiajie is jaw-dropping as you ascend from city streets into mountain clouds. The 999 steps to Heaven's Gate (Tianmen Cave) are a memorable physical challenge. The glass skywalks bolted onto sheer cliff faces provide heart-pounding moments even for non-acrophobic visitors. The 99-bend mountain road is an engineering wonder. However, this is a heavily managed, theme-park-style mountain experience — you're funneled along set routes with escalators, shuttle buses, and crowd management. Fog frequently obscures views, and the glass skywalks are less dramatic in poor visibility. Lines for the cable car can exceed an hour during peak times. The ¥288 ticket is expensive by Chinese standards but covers cable car, buses, and all attractions. Best for thrill-seekers and visitors who want dramatic mountain scenery without serious hiking.

foreigner_top_questions.question: Which route (A, B, or C) should I choose?
foreigner_top_questions.answer: Route A (recommended for most): Take the long cable car up (7.5 km, spectacular), walk the summit skywalks, descend to Tianmen Cave via escalators, climb down the 999 steps (easier than climbing up), take the coach down the 99-bend road. This gives you the best experiences in order. Route B: Coach up the 99-bend road, fast cable car to summit, walk skywalks, long cable car down. Route C: Fast cable car both ways (best for motion sickness sufferers, skips the 99-bend road). Route A typically has longer queues in the morning but is the most dramatic sequence.

foreigner_top_questions.question: Do I need to book in advance?
foreigner_top_questions.answer: Yes — Tianmen Mountain uses a mandatory real-name, time-slot reservation system. Walk-in tickets are NOT available. Book online via the official WeChat mini-program or Trip.com/Klook at least 1-2 days in advance. Peak season and holidays sell out days ahead. Choose a morning time slot (8:00-8:30 AM) for shorter queues and better weather odds. If the booking system is giving you trouble or you're unsure which route to pick, our concierge team can book it for you and recommend the best route based on your fitness level and schedule.

experience_format_note: Full-day managed mountain attraction. The ¥288 ticket includes: cable car ride(s), eco-coach transport, summit access, glass skywalks, Tianmen Cave access, and escalators. The only additional costs are shoe covers for glass skywalks (¥5) and optional guide (¥200). The experience follows a set route (A, B, or C) that takes 4-6 hours. Real-name time-slot booking is mandatory.
vibe: A blockbuster nature-meets-engineering spectacle — like the mountain equivalent of a theme park ride, but the mountain is genuinely 1,519 meters tall and the glass is genuinely over a 300-meter drop.

time_needed.quick_visit: 3-4 hours (one route, moving quickly through viewpoints)
time_needed.recommended: 5-6 hours (one route with time at all viewpoints, Tianmen Cave, and glass skywalks)
time_needed.deep_dive: Full day (explore both east and west summit trails, linger at viewpoints, take photos)

best_time.best_time_of_day: Arrive at opening (8:00 AM) to avoid the worst queues and have the best chance of clear weather before afternoon clouds roll in. Early morning light on the mountain is also the most photogenic.
best_time.worst_time: Chinese holidays and weekends — cable car queues can exceed 2 hours. Afternoon on most days when clouds/fog typically roll in. Winter when some facilities close due to ice.
best_time.seasonal_notes: Spring and autumn offer the best weather — clear skies and comfortable temperatures. Summer has dramatic cloud formations but heavy rain. Winter brings stunning ice and snow scenery but glass skywalks and some trails may close for safety. The mountain summit is always significantly cooler than the city below.
best_time.pro_tip: Book the earliest time slot (8:00 AM). If the morning starts foggy, don't despair — mountain weather changes rapidly and fog often clears by mid-morning, revealing dramatic views.

getting_in.opening_hours: 8:00 AM - 7:00 PM (entry closes at 4:00 PM). Hours vary seasonally — check before visiting. Some facilities close in winter due to ice.
getting_in.price_rmb: ¥288 (full ticket including all transport). Glass skywalk shoe covers: ¥5.

price_breakdown.highlight: Includes cable car, coach, summit access, glass skywalks, escalators, Tianmen Cave
Required to walk on the glass sections — purchased on-site
Full-route guided interpretation available at the cable car station

getting_in.booking_required: Yes — mandatory real-name time-slot reservation. No walk-in tickets. Book 1-2 days ahead minimum; holidays require earlier booking.
getting_in.booking_method: Official WeChat mini-program or Trip.com/Klook. Passport number required. Select route (A/B/C) and time slot during booking.
getting_in.passport_accepted: Yes — foreigners book with passport number. Children under 14 with valid ID enter free. Seniors 60+ and students get discounted tickets.
getting_in.what_to_bring: Warm jacket (summit is 10-15°C cooler than the city). Rain jacket. Comfortable shoes with grip. Water. Snacks. Camera. Passport for ID check.
getting_in.queue_situation: Cable car queues: 30-60 minutes typical, 2+ hours on holidays. The VIP fast-track option costs extra but skips the queue. Escalator queues inside the mountain are usually 10-20 minutes.
getting_in.language_barrier_rating: some-chinese-helps — Route signage has some English. The cable car and bus staff speak Chinese only. The experience is largely visual and doesn't require much verbal communication, but having a translation app helps for route choices and any issues.

highlights.name: Tianmen Mountain Cable Car (天门山索道)
highlights.description: The world's longest single-section cable car at 7,455 meters, ascending 1,279 meters from downtown Zhangjiajie to the mountain summit in about 28 minutes. The ride passes over the city, then through forests, and finally through cloud layers — an experience in itself.
highlights.foreigner_note: This is not a short scenic gondola — it's a 28-minute journey that feels like ascending into another world. The transition from urban streets to mountain wilderness is surreal.
highlights.tip: Sit on the side facing the mountain (right side going up) for the best views. The cable car gondolas hold 8 people. Bring a jacket — it gets cold at altitude.

highlights.name: Tianmen Cave — Heaven's Gate (天门洞)
highlights.description: A massive natural cave opening (131.5 meters high, 57 meters wide) that pierces completely through the mountain. Formed by geological collapse during the Three Kingdoms period (263 AD), it was seen as an auspicious omen. Reaching it requires climbing the famous 999 steps — a steep, dramatic staircase.
highlights.foreigner_note: The 999 steps (representing 'nine heavens' in Chinese numerology) are the most photographed feature of the mountain. Climbing them feels like ascending to heaven — and it's genuinely exhausting. You can also reach the cave via escalators if you prefer.
highlights.tip: Descending the steps (from the escalator exit down to the bus platform) is easier than climbing up. Take it slow on the steeper upper sections and use the railings. The cave itself is most dramatic when clouds drift through it.

highlights.name: Glass Skywalks (玻璃栈道)
highlights.description: Three sections of transparent glass walkways bolted onto the sheer cliff face at about 1,400 meters elevation. The glass is beneath your feet with 300+ meters of empty air below. The Coiling Dragon Cliff section on the east side is the most dramatic.
highlights.foreigner_note: You must wear shoe covers (¥5) to protect the glass. The walkways are perfectly safe but genuinely thrilling — even people without fear of heights find their knees weakening. On foggy days, the glass effect is diminished as you can't see the drop.
highlights.tip: The east side glass walk (Coiling Dragon Cliff) is longer and more dramatic than the west side. Visit on a clear day to see the full drop beneath your feet.

highlights.name: 99-Bend Tongtian Avenue (通天大道)
highlights.description: A 10.77-kilometer mountain road with 99 hairpin turns that switchbacks from 200m to 1,300m elevation. The road itself is an engineering marvel, and riding the coach through the turns is a white-knuckle experience. The aerial view from the cable car shows the entire road snaking up the mountain like a ribbon.
highlights.foreigner_note: The bus drivers are incredibly skilled, navigating blind 180-degree turns with centimeters of clearance. Route A includes riding down this road by coach — it's equal parts terrifying and impressive.
highlights.tip: Sit on the left side of the coach for the best views of the cliff drops. The ride takes about 25 minutes. Motion sickness pills recommended for sensitive travelers.

what_visitors_miss.what: Both the east AND west summit trails
what_visitors_miss.why: Many visitors only walk one side due to time pressure. Both the east trail (with the Coiling Dragon glass walk) and west trail (with different viewpoints and its own glass section) are worth walking — each offers distinct perspectives. Budget an extra hour to do both.
A Buddhist temple at the summit that most visitors rush past. It's a peaceful counterpoint to the adrenaline of the glass walks, with mountain views from its courtyards.

strategy.smart_route: Book Route A with earliest time slot (8:00 AM) → take the long cable car up (28 minutes, spectacular) → explore BOTH east and west summit trails including glass skywalks → descend via escalators to Tianmen Cave → climb down the 999 steps (easier than climbing up) → take coach down the 99-bend road → return to city. Total: 5-6 hours.
strategy.what_to_skip: The overpriced summit restaurants — bring your own food and water. The photo spots where staff take your picture and charge ¥20-50 for prints.
strategy.pro_tips: Wear layers you can remove — you'll be hot climbing the 999 steps but cold on the windy summit. The escalators inside the mountain are the longest in the world and are included in your ticket — ride them for the experience alone. If fog blocks views on the summit, the glass walks and Tianmen Cave are still impressive.

heads_up.advice: The mountain creates its own weather. Clear skies in the city below don't guarantee clear views at the summit. Mornings are generally clearer than afternoons. If fog is thick, the glass walks lose their dramatic effect since you can't see the drop.

The steps are steep and relentless, especially the upper half. Escalators are available as an alternative for the upper section. Descending is much easier than ascending. Bring water and take breaks. If you're feeling wrecked afterward, message our team — we can book a nearby spa or have a taxi waiting for you at the coach drop-off point.

Glass skywalks, some trails, and the 99-bend road may close when ice forms (typically December-February). Route C (fast cable car only) may be the only option. The winter snow scenery is beautiful but access is limited.
The coach ride through 99 hairpin turns causes motion sickness in many visitors. Take medication before the ride if you're sensitive. Route C avoids the road entirely.

foreigners_watch_out: Tickets MUST be booked online in advance with passport number — there are no walk-in tickets. Book at least 1-2 days ahead, more during holidays. If you're struggling with the booking system or can't figure out which route and time slot to pick, our concierge can handle it — message us with your travel date.

The cable car station is in downtown Zhangjiajie city (NOT in Wulingyuan/the National Forest Park area). It's a different attraction from Zhangjiajie National Forest Park and requires a separate ticket.
The summit is 10-15°C colder than the city — bring warm clothing even in summer. Wind chill on exposed glass walks makes it feel even colder.
Route selection (A/B/C) is made at booking time and cannot be changed on-site. Research routes before booking.

if_things_go_wrong.problem: Cable car closed due to wind or storms
if_things_go_wrong.what_to_do: Closures are announced at the station. Your ticket can be refunded or rescheduled. Check weather before heading to the station.
if_things_go_wrong.plan_b: Visit Zhangjiajie National Forest Park (Wulingyuan) instead — it's a different attraction 40 minutes away that operates in most weather conditions. Message us and we can rebook your Tianmen tickets for another day and arrange transport to the forest park instead.

if_things_go_wrong.problem: Glass skywalks closed due to ice or weather
if_things_go_wrong.what_to_do: The summit trails are still walkable (with regular paved sections instead of glass). Tianmen Cave and the cable car still operate in most conditions.
if_things_go_wrong.plan_b: The summit forest trails, Tianmen Cave, and cable car alone are still worth the visit — the glass walks are exciting but not the only attraction.

preparation.what_to_wear: Layers — warm for the summit, lighter for the 999 steps. Non-slip shoes essential (glass walks and stone steps can be slippery). Rain jacket. Wind-proof jacket for summit.
preparation.what_to_bring: Warm jacket. Rain gear. Water (at least 1 liter). Snacks. Camera. Passport. Motion sickness medication if prone. Cash for shoe covers (¥5).
preparation.what_not_to_bring: Large bags (luggage storage available at the cable car station, ¥5-10). Heels or sandals. Selfie sticks may be restricted on glass walks.

physical_accessibility.physical_details: The cable car and escalators make much of the mountain accessible without hiking. Summit trails are paved with some stairs. The 999 steps to Tianmen Cave are very strenuous (can be avoided via escalators). Glass walks are flat but exposed to heights.
physical_accessibility.age_notes: Children over 6 can enjoy most of the experience. Elderly visitors can use escalators to avoid the 999 steps. The cable car is suitable for all ages. Not recommended for those with severe fear of heights.
physical_accessibility.health_warnings: Heart conditions: consult a doctor before the 999-step climb. Motion sickness: the 99-bend road and cable car can trigger nausea. Heights anxiety: the glass walks are not mandatory — you can use the regular paved trail sections instead.

concierge_opportunities.action: Book Tianmen Mountain tickets with correct route and time slot
concierge_opportunities.value_to_user: Solves the complex booking process — route selection, time slot, and passport entry handled for you. English-language booking interface. Some packages include guide service.

pair_with.suggestion: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park (张家界国家森林公园)
pair_with.why: The other essential Zhangjiajie experience — Avatar-inspiring sandstone pillars, Golden Whip Stream, Tianzi Mountain. A completely different landscape from Tianmen Mountain. Plan 2-3 separate days.
pair_with.travel_time: 40 minutes by bus from Zhangjiajie city to Wulingyuan entrance

pair_with.why: If you enjoyed the glass skywalks, the world's highest and longest glass bridge offers an even more dramatic glass experience over a canyon.

cultural_context: Tianmen Cave is revered in Chinese culture as a gateway to heaven — its formation in 263 AD (when part of the mountain collapsed creating the hole) was recorded in historical texts as a divine omen during the Three Kingdoms period. The name 'Heaven's Gate' reflects the Taoist belief that the mountain connects earth and sky. The 999 steps encode the number 9, which represents the highest single digit and is associated with the emperor and heaven in Chinese numerology.

photo_spots.location: Cable car approaching the mountain wall
photo_spots.tip: Have camera ready during the final 5 minutes of the cable car ride as you approach the cliff face — the mountain looms dramatically ahead.
photo_spots.why: The transition from floating over forest to confronting a sheer rock wall is the most dramatic moment of the cable car ride.

photo_spots.tip: Photograph from about halfway down the steps looking up — this gives the classic perspective of the massive cave opening with steps leading into it.
photo_spots.why: The iconic Tianmen Mountain image — the enormous natural hole in the mountain with the dramatic staircase ascending into clouds.

photo_spots.location: Glass skywalk on the east side (Coiling Dragon Cliff)
photo_spots.tip: Clear day required for the full effect. Look straight down through the glass for vertigo-inducing shots of the 300m drop.
photo_spots.why: The most dramatic selfie location on the mountain — transparent glass floor with nothing but air below your feet.

card_hook: Climb 999 steps to walk through a hole in the sky.
